sessions.session_title: Check-in conversation – brief status update (Daisy Boynton)
sessions.notes_text:
Follow-Up Call: Tyshawn Smith
Date: 11/3/2026 | Staff: Daisy | Type: Phone follow-up to the 11/2 consultation
Outcome: Told him he’ll need to complete a recovery program before joining First Shift. After pushing back for a while, he agreed to do it. Daisy will send him (1) low-cost or free recovery program options in his area and (2) second chance job openings, both this week.

Call Summary

Explained that no exception was granted, so completing a recovery program is required before he can start.
He disputed that he has an alcohol problem. He said he only drinks on weekends, not every day, that “everybody drinks,” and that what he shared yesterday was about his past (“not is, but was”). Later in the call he said, “I had a problem. I didn’t deal with the problem. I’m dealing with the problem still.”
He feels he’s being punished for being honest (“I should have just kept my mouth closed”) and “treated like an alcoholic.”
He asked whether he’d have to stop drinking completely. Daisy said Turn90 can’t control what he does, but the recovery program is required to join.
He said he’s overwhelmed right now.
He brought up re-enrolling in ADSAP, which he estimated at about $500. Daisy noted he’d already finished ADSAP and said she’d look for options that are free or low-cost.
He asked how long a recovery program takes. Daisy didn’t know yet and said it depends on the program.
Offered a second path: if his main goal is a job, Daisy can send second chance job openings, and he wouldn’t need the recovery program for that.
He asked whether Turn90 can guarantee him a job after the program. Daisy answered, “I could guarantee that, yes.”
He ended by agreeing to the classes and asked for the second chance job openings too.

Next Steps

Daisy (this week): Research recovery programs near him that are free or low-cost, outpatient or residential, and send him options with how long each one takes.
Daisy (this week): Send him second chance job openings.
After he finishes a program: Revisit his First Shift enrollment and finish the rest of his consultation (justice history, education and work).
Still open from 11/2: medical, dental and vision referrals, his ADSAP paperwork and ticket for the license, and housing stability.

sessions.notes_text:
Intake Screening: Tyshawn Smith
Date: 11/2/2026 | Staff: Daisy | Type: Phone consultation (Columbia), not finished
Outcome: Eligibility for First Shift is on hold. He reported heavy, recent alcohol use (most recent drink was recent) and has never completed a treatment program. Under current policy, he’d need to complete a substance use program before starting in person. He asked for an exception. Daisy will talk to the program manager and call him back later today or tomorrow (by 11/3) at the latest.

Call Notes

His consultation was scheduled for 11 AM. He thought it was at 10, so he missed your first call, and you did the consultation on the callback.
He was new to Turn90, so you went over both First Shift (Columbia) and reentry navigation.

Housing

He currently has a place to stay. He said it depends on a relationship that’s going through “a little thing,” so he couldn’t say whether it’s stable long-term.
Told him we can help with housing if he needs it.

Documents

State ID, birth certificate, Social Security card: Yes, he has all of them.
Driver’s license: Not yet valid. He owes about $170–175 for a speeding ticket from Aiken, SC. He recently finished ADSAP, but the program hadn’t sent the completion paperwork to the DMV. He contacted them about a week ago and hasn’t checked back with the DMV since.

Transportation

Rides the bus. Told him the nearest stop is a 15–20 minute walk from the Columbia center.
Plans to buy an e-bike in about 2 weeks to cover the gap between the bus and where he needs to go.
Whether family can drive him wasn’t clear.

Availability

No conflicts with 9–3, Monday through Friday.

Health

Prescribed Remeron while incarcerated. He doesn’t need it now.
He named health concerns as emergency needs:
Lower back pain that sometimes runs down the back of his leg
A large cavity or hole in an upper back tooth on the right side
Vision getting blurry
These may call for medical, dental and vision referrals.

Substance Use

Describes himself as a heavy alcohol user and an alcoholic, with alcoholism in his family. Drinks mostly wine. No problems with other drugs besides marijuana.
Says he now drinks mainly on weekends, not every day. He drank recently.
Says alcohol has been involved in his incarceration, in falling out with family and his kids, and in violence when he feels disrespected.
Says he drinks to “self-medicate” because he has no motivation or structure right now. He’s been filling out applications and going to job fairs, keeps getting turned down, and feels overwhelmed.
He’s never completed a substance use program. He said he’s open to one.
He says alcohol has never caused him trouble at a job (never fired or written up for it).

Program Conversation

Explained that applicants with recent use need to finish a substance use program (residential or outpatient) before First Shift. That’s because it’s only 8 weeks before job placement, and employer partners trust Turn90 to send people who are ready.
Made clear this delays his start but doesn’t shut him out. Offered help finding a program, plus resumes, job search and other support in the meantime.
He pushed back. He feels he was being honest and is now penalized for it (“I really should have told you I wasn’t drinking”), and he sees this program as his chance (“without y’all right now, I’m going back to square one”).
He said he’d go along with whatever is required (“whatever y’all commit me to do, I’m with it”).

Next Steps

Daisy: Call Tyshawn back later today or tomorrow, by 11/3.
If no exception: Find him a recovery program (outpatient or residential) through community partners, and enroll him in reentry navigation while he waits.
Either way: Follow up on medical, dental and vision referrals, his ADSAP paperwork and ticket for the license, and housing stability.
Finish the consultation: justice history, supervision, pending charges, child support, education, work history and certifications.
